project.name: SnapTrack
project.description: Studio 94 SnapTrack — a procedural PHP/MySQL photography studio management and booking system. Single index.php router dispatches role-based pages (admin, staff, client) rendered as server-side PHP with vanilla JS/CSS. Handles bookings, payments, inventory, loyalty tiers, feedback with Gemini AI analysis, MFA/TOTP and Google OAuth auth, PHPMailer/Resend email, and web push notifications. Deployed via Nixpacks to Railway.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Template environment file documenting all 18 runtime variables consumed by config.php: app URL, MySQL credentials, VAPID web-push keys, PayMongo and Google OAuth secrets, the Gemini API key, SMTP credentials, and a Resend key. Values here are placeholders only and are read by the hand-rolled loadEnv() in config.php, which populates $_ENV and putenv().
nodes.languageNotes: config.php falls back to Railway-style MYSQLHOST/MYSQLPORT/MYSQLDATABASE/MYSQLUSER/MYSQLPASSWORD when the DB_* keys above are unset, so this file is the primary local-dev path and the platform vars override it in production.

nodes.name: AGENTS.md
nodes.summary: Agent-facing engineering notes for SnapTrack covering setup commands, the index.php?page= router and its $rolePages allowlist, env/config caveats, the runtime schema mutation in ensureDatabaseSchema(), and known gotchas. Documents that pages/<role>/*.php are not standalone, the root styles.css is dead, and display_errors is off so fatals surface as a blank page logged to php-errors.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Eight sections including a 'Gotchas' list that flags dead code (root styles.css, PACKAGES/LOYALTY_TIERS constants), silently no-opping push notifications, and scattered upload directories.

nodes.name: GEMINI.md
nodes.summary: Project context document for Studio 94 SnapTrack describing the PHP 8.1 / MySQL stack, the role-based pages/ layout (admin, staff, client, api), and the external integrations (Gemini AI, Google OAuth + TOTP MFA, PayMongo, PHPMailer, Resend, QR codes, TCPDF/FPDF). Includes installation steps, coding-style conventions, responsive breakpoints, and Nixpacks/Railway deployment notes.

nodes.name: composer.json
nodes.summary: Composer manifest pinning PHP >=8.1 and the pdo, pdo_mysql, mysqli extensions, plus three runtime packages: google/apiclient 2.15.0, phpmailer/phpmailer ^7.1, and endroid/qr-code ^6.0. Notably it has no autoload section, which is why the project's dependency graph is expressed entirely through manual require_once calls rather than PSR-4 autoloading.
nodes.languageNotes: The absence of an autoload block is why vendor/ is required at runtime yet no import edges resolve automatically; minishlink/web-push is missing here, which is why sendPushNotification() silently no-ops.

nodes.name: nixpacks.toml
nodes.summary: Two-line Nixpacks configuration declaring the PHP extensions to install in the build image: mysqli, pdo_mysql, pdo, gd, curl, and mbstring. This is what makes the Railway deployment image able to serve the app at all, since the base PHP image omits gd and curl.

nodes.name: app.js
nodes.summary: The live ~126-line frontend utility layer providing sidebar toggling, toast notifications, table filtering, modal helpers, form validation and print-section support. Loaded once by footer.php.

nodes.name: .gitkeep

nodes.name: change_password.php
nodes.summary: One-shot destructive ops script that resets every row of the users table to a freshly generated hash of the literal password "password" and prints the result. Web-accessible and referenced by nothing -- must be deleted before any real deploy.
nodes.languageNotes: Executes top-level procedural code on include (no function wrapper or guard), so merely fetching the URL rewrites the whole users table.

nodes.name: config.php
nodes.summary: Central configuration bootstrap: hand-rolled .env loading, database constants with Railway MYSQL* fallbacks, APP_URL auto-detection, upload/session paths, Gemini and Gmail/Resend mail settings, and the PHP error-logging policy.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses $_ENV-then-getenv() null-coalescing chains; note GEMINI_MODEL, MAIL_HOST, MAIL_PORT, UPLOAD_DIR and SESSION_LIFETIME are hardcoded define()s that .env cannot override, and base-path detection only special-cases /snaptrack.

nodes.name: showToast
nodes.summary: Builds a self-styled toast with per-type colour and emoji, injects its keyframe animation once, then fades and removes itself after three seconds.

nodes.name: validateForm
nodes.summary: Checks every [required] field in a form, flagging empty ones with the error border and returning overall validity.

nodes.name: printSection
nodes.summary: Opens a print window containing a single element innerHTML, links the live stylesheet using a /snaptrack-aware base path and triggers the print dialog.

nodes.name: loadEnv
nodes.summary: Minimal .env parser that skips comments and blank lines, splits KEY=VALUE pairs, strips surrounding quotes and republishes each value into both $_ENV and putenv.
nodes.languageNotes: A hand-rolled replacement for phpdotenv with no multiline, export or escape handling, and no override protection -- last occurrence in the file wins.

nodes.name: footer.php

nodes.languageNotes: Mixed PHP/HTML/CSS/JS partial whose role-gated blocks depend on $role being defined by index.php before inclusion.

nodes.name: functions.php
nodes.summary: Core procedural helper library and the single shared function surface for the whole app: PDO connection with runtime schema auto-migration, auth/CSRF/flash, notifications, Web Push, loyalty tiers, inventory and view helpers. Required by virtually every page and API endpoint.
nodes.languageNotes: 61 global functions, no classes and no Composer autoload: sharing relies entirely on `require_once __DIR__ . '/functions.php'`. db() memoizes the PDO handle and fires ensureDatabaseSchema() on first call, so the app mutates its own schema at runtime.

nodes.name: google-callback.php
nodes.summary: OAuth2 callback endpoint for Google Sign-In: exchanges the auth code for a token via google/apiclient, rejects non-Gmail addresses, auto-creates or email-verifies the user, regenerates the session and redirects into the routed dashboard. Appends verbose traces to google-debug.log.
nodes.languageNotes: Inverts the project-wide error policy by setting display_errors ON and echoing raw exception text, whereas config.php disables display_errors so fatals render as a blank page.

nodes.name: google-config.php
nodes.summary: Defines GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET and GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI from environment variables, delegating to config.php for env loading and the APP_URL-based redirect default. Shared by the Google sign-in start and callback scripts.

nodes.name: google-login.php
nodes.summary: Entry point that initiates the Google OAuth2 authorization-code flow by redirecting to Google's auth endpoint. Bails out to login.php with a session error when the client credentials are absent from the environment.

nodes.name: header.php
nodes.summary: Shared HTML <head> partial included by index.php: emits the page title through clean(), links assets/css/styles.css and opens the app-layout wrapper. Not standalone — it needs config.php's APP_URL and functions.php's clean() already loaded by the router.

nodes.name: booking.php
nodes.summary: Booking persistence helpers used by the SnapBot chatbot, each with a JSON-file fallback. BROKEN: saveBooking/getBookings/getBookingStats call getDBConnection(), which is defined nowhere in the project (the only accessor is db() in functions.php), and the file never requires functions.php for the addNotificationByRole() calls it makes.
nodes.languageNotes: Branches to saveBookingToFile() on PDOException, but the undefined getDBConnection() raises a PHP Error that is not caught, so the JSON fallback path is effectively unreachable.

nodes.name: chatbot.php
nodes.summary: Self-contained 'SnapBot AI' chat widget (CSS + HTML + vanilla JS) injected into client pages by footer.php, with a draggable panel, quick replies, localStorage chat history and POSTs to pages/api/chatbot-ai.php. Contains no PHP logic and no require statements.

nodes.name: startSession
nodes.summary: Starts the PHP session with configured cookie parameters and the session lifetime defined in config.php.

nodes.name: currentUser
nodes.summary: Loads the authenticated user record for the current session, returning null when nobody is logged in.

nodes.name: db
nodes.summary: Lazily creates and memoizes the shared PDO handle with emulated prepares disabled and exception error mode, then triggers ensureDatabaseSchema() on first call. Renders a styled setup hint and dies on connection failure.

nodes.name: ensureDatabaseSchema
nodes.summary: Runtime schema auto-migration guard: inspects users, bookings, payments and packages, ALTERs in any missing columns, MODIFYs the booking status and payment type/status ENUMs, and creates the password_resets table. Guarded by a static flag and swallows failures to the error log.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs on the first db() call of every request, so the app needs ALTER privileges in production and ENUM changes must be mirrored in sql/install.sql or fresh and migrated installs diverge.

nodes.name: requireRole
nodes.summary: Authorizes the current session against one or more roles (case-insensitive) and redirects to the dashboard rather than the login page on failure. The access-control gate called by every page under pages/<role>/.

nodes.name: redirectToDashboard

nodes.name: csrfToken
nodes.summary: Returns the session's CSRF token, generating and storing one on first use.

nodes.name: verifyCsrf
nodes.summary: Compares the submitted CSRF token against the session value and rejects the request on mismatch.

nodes.name: getFlash
nodes.summary: Reads the pending flash message from the session, returning null when none is queued.

nodes.name: showFlash
nodes.summary: Renders the stored flash message as styled HTML and clears it from the session in the same step.

nodes.name: timeAgo

nodes.name: statusBadge

nodes.name: addNotification

nodes.name: addNotificationByRole

nodes.name: getUnreadCount

nodes.name: getNotifications

nodes.name: getNotification

nodes.name: sendPushNotification

nodes.name: getLoyaltyRewards
nodes.summary: Returns the list of rewards unlocked at a given completed-booking count using the 2/4/7/10 thresholds.

nodes.name: checkBookingConflict
nodes.summary: Detects overlapping bookings for a given date and time by comparing each booking's start against its duration, optionally excluding the booking currently being edited.

nodes.name: isSlotAvailable
nodes.summary: Convenience wrapper reporting whether a requested date and time slot is free for a given package.

nodes.name: getBookingStatusBadge
nodes.summary: Maps a booking status to its badge label and colour, supplying the data that statusBadge() wraps in markup.

nodes.name: paginate
nodes.summary: Computes pagination window metadata — total pages, current range and previous/next flags — for list views.

nodes.name: outputCSV
nodes.summary: Streams rows to the browser as a downloadable CSV file given headers, rows and a filename.

nodes.name: uploadFile
nodes.summary: Validates an uploaded file's type against an allowlist, generates a safe unique filename and moves it into the target directory.

nodes.name: getPackageInventory
nodes.summary: Joins package_inventory with inventory to return the stock items a package consumes, with quantities, thresholds and reusability flags.

nodes.name: deductInventoryOnComplete
nodes.summary: Consumes a package's inventory when a booking completes: opens a transaction, row-locks each inventory record with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, skips reusable items, writes booking_inventory audit rows and reports deducted/skipped/error detail, rolling back on failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses SELECT ... FOR UPDATE inside an explicit transaction to make concurrent stock deduction safe.

nodes.name: restoreInventory
nodes.summary: Reverses a completed deduction in a transaction — adds quantities back to non-reusable inventory and deletes the booking_inventory audit rows.

nodes.name: checkLowStockAndNotify
nodes.summary: Scans inventory for quantities at or below their configured threshold and raises admin notifications for low stock.

nodes.name: saveBooking
nodes.summary: Persists a chatbot booking: finds or creates the user, resolves the package (with a LIKE match and a default fallback), generates a booking reference, computes the 50% deposit and remaining balance, inserts the booking plus a DEPOSIT payment row, ensures a loyalty card exists and notifies admin and staff. Falls back to saveBookingToFile() on PDOException.
nodes.languageNotes: Calls getDBConnection(), which is undefined project-wide, so this function fatals before reaching its JSON fallback; the catch block only handles PDOException, not Error.

nodes.name: saveBookingToFile
nodes.summary: JSON-file fallback that appends a booking to data/bookings.json, creating the data directory on demand.

nodes.name: getBookings
nodes.summary: Returns bookings joined with users and packages, optionally filtered by status, and returns an empty array when the query fails.

nodes.name: getBookingStats
nodes.summary: Aggregates booking counts per status plus total revenue across non-cancelled bookings, degrading to an all-zero array on failure.

nodes.name: getBookingStatsFromFile
nodes.summary: Backward-compatibility alias that computes per-status booking counts from the JSON file instead of the database.

nodes.name: deduct_inventory.php
nodes.summary: Standalone inventory-deduction helper that maps a package name to consumable/reusable item quantities, decrements stock on booking completion, and raises low-stock notifications. It is never `require`d or `include`d anywhere in the repository, so these two functions are currently unreachable dead code; the live equivalent is `deductInventoryOnComplete()` in `functions.php`.
nodes.languageNotes: Package-to-item mapping is hardcoded as a literal array keyed by the packages.name string, so renaming a package in the DB silently disables its deductions. Because the file has no require of functions.php, it depends on the caller having already loaded config.php/functions.php and passes the PDO handle in explicitly.

nodes.name: deductInventory
nodes.summary: Resolves the package name, looks it up in a hardcoded package-to-inventory map, decrements consumable stock via prepared statements, records reusable-item bookings, and notifies admin/staff when an item drops to its threshold. Returns a structured success/message/deducted/reusable/errors array and appends a line to `logs/inventory.log`.

nodes.name: recordReusableItemUsage
nodes.summary: Logs a reusable inventory item's usage against a booking by inserting a row into `booking_inventory` with the current timestamp.

nodes.name: index.php
nodes.summary: The single router and authenticated entry point for all SnapTrack UI (`index.php?page=<name>`). It loads config.php/functions.php, re-reads and re-validates the user from the DB on every request, validates the requested page against the per-role `$rolePages` allowlist, resolves the page file through a fallback chain (own role dir -> `pages/<page>.php` -> other role dirs -> shared `walkin.php` -> dashboard), then wraps it in header/sidebar/footer with the photography-themed topbar CSS.
nodes.languageNotes: Purely procedural PHP with no functions or classes: all control flow is top-level `if`/redirect/`require`. Two silent-failure behaviours matter here — a page missing from `$rolePages` is replaced with `dashboard` with no user-visible error (only `error_log`), and an unresolvable page file returns a hand-written 500 HTML page. Note it uses `session_start()` directly rather than `startSession()` from functions.php.

nodes.name: landing.php
nodes.summary: Public marketing landing page for STUDIO 94 self-shoot studio. Requires config.php/functions.php, branches its call-to-action links based on `isLoggedIn()` and session role (clients go to `index.php?page=booking`, staff/admin to `page=walkin`, anonymous users are sent through `login.php?redirect=...`), and embeds roughly 470 lines of inline CSS/HTML/JS for the hero, package tiers, and how-it-works sections.
nodes.languageNotes: Almost the entire file is inline `<style>` and markup rather than PHP — the only PHP is the 25-line auth-aware link computation at the top, so the file is mostly a static template with a dynamic header.

nodes.name: login.php
nodes.summary: Combined login / register / forgot-password / reset-password page that is the app's authentication entry point. A single CSRF-protected POST handler dispatches on a hidden `action` field: `login` (Gmail-only regex check, `password_verify`, refuses unverified email, `session_regenerate_id`), `register` (creates or refreshes an unverified client, sends a verification email and auto-verifies on 'skipped'/'failed' delivery), `forgot_password` (inserts a `password_resets` row and mails a link) and `reset_password` (consumes the token and rehashes the password).
nodes.languageNotes: Gmail-only policy is enforced twice — server-side via `preg_match('/@gmail\.com$/i')` and client-side via an HTML `pattern` attribute. The register branch silently auto-verifies the account when SMTP is unconfigured or blocked, so the email-verification gate is effectively bypassed on hosts without working mail.

nodes.name: logout.php
nodes.summary: Minimal session teardown endpoint that clears `$_SESSION`, expires the session cookie using the existing cookie params, destroys the session, and redirects to `login.php`. It requires only `functions.php` and relies on that file transitively loading `config.php` for the `APP_URL` constant.

nodes.name: mfa-helper.php
nodes.summary: Dependency-free TOTP (RFC 6238) implementation wrapped in the `MFAHelper` class — base32 secret generation/decoding, HOTP code derivation, constant-time verification with time-slice discrepancy tolerance, `otpauth://` URI building, QR code rendering via `endroid/qr-code`, and bcrypt-hashed single-use backup codes. Included only by `mfa-setup.php`.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-rolled TOTP so no Composer package is required: the base32 alphabet, HMAC-SHA1 truncation and dynamic-truncation bit extraction are all implemented inline with `hash_hmac` and `ord`. `getQRCodeDataURI()` falls back to the raw `otpauth://` URI when the optional `endroid/qr-code` classes are absent.

nodes.name: MFAHelper
nodes.summary: Static utility class holding the full TOTP two-factor flow: `generateSecret`, `base32Decode` (private), `generateCode`, `verifyCode`, `getOTPAuthURI`, `getQRCodeDataURI`, `generateBackupCodes`, `hashBackupCodes` and `verifyBackupCode`. No state is kept — every method is a pure function of its arguments.

nodes.name: base32Decode
nodes.summary: Private helper converting an RFC 4648 base32 TOTP secret into raw binary bytes, stripping padding/whitespace and packing leftover bits into a final character.

nodes.name: generateCode
nodes.summary: Derives a 6-digit HOTP code for a given time slice by HMAC-SHA1 hashing the 8-byte counter, applying dynamic truncation, and zero-padding the result.

nodes.name: verifyCode
nodes.summary: Validates a submitted 6-digit TOTP code against the secret, comparing the current and adjacent time slices with `hash_equals()` to tolerate modest device clock drift.

nodes.name: getQRCodeDataURI
nodes.summary: Renders the `otpauth://` provisioning URI as a base64 PNG data URI for inline `` display using endroid/qr-code, logging and degrading to the raw URI if the optional library is not installed.

nodes.name: verifyBackupCode
nodes.summary: Checks a user-supplied recovery code against the bcrypt hashes stored as a JSON array on the user row, and returns the rewritten hash list with the consumed code removed.

nodes.name: mfa-setup.php
nodes.summary: Standalone two-factor enrollment page that sits outside the router: a CSRF-protected POST handler supports `generate` (stash a new secret in the session and re-render the QR), `verify` (confirm the first TOTP code, persist `mfa_enabled`/`mfa_secret`/hashed backup codes, then show the codes once), and `disable` (requires re-entering the account password). Renders one of four states — backup codes, QR scan, enabled, disabled — depending on `?step=`, the pending session secret, and the stored `mfa_enabled` flag.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses POST-redirect-GET so the enrollment step is driven by `?step=` plus session state rather than by re-POSTing, and unsets `$_SESSION['new_backup_codes']` inline in the template so plaintext recovery codes are shown exactly once.

nodes.name: DFD.HTML
nodes.summary: Static 1800x1200 inline-SVG data-flow diagram titled 'Studio 94 DFD Layout' that maps the system's entities (Client, Studio Staff, Studio Owner), processes 1.0-8.0 (authentication, booking, service, inventory, AI chatbot, payment, feedback, reports) and data stores D1-D7. It contains no PHP and is dead: the `.HTML` extension means `index.php`'s router (which always appends `.php`) can never reach it, and nothing else links to it. Valuable only as design documentation of the intended system.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-positioned SVG rects/text rather than a diagram DSL or Mermaid source, so the layout cannot be regenerated from a text definition — edits mean editing raw x/y coordinates.

nodes.name: bookings.php
nodes.summary: Admin read-only bookings listing page. Builds a dynamic WHERE clause from the `status` and `q` query params, then runs a prepared statement joining bookings to users and packages with a correlated subquery that counts `booking_inventory` rows per booking; results are ordered newest-first and rendered as a table with client, package, schedule, type, inventory count and status badges. Deliberately exposes no status-mutation controls — an inline banner states admins may view but not approve, complete or cancel bookings, which is staff-only. Not a standalone script: the bare `requireRole('admin')` on line 2 assumes `index.php` has already loaded config.php/functions.php and defined the role, page and user variables, so opening the file directly is a fatal error.
nodes.languageNotes: Pure procedural PHP with no class or function declarations. Every SQL value is bound through a `?` placeholder because `db()` sets `ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false`, and all echoed values pass through `clean()` for output escaping.

nodes.name: clients.php
nodes.summary: Admin client directory page: one un-paginated query joins users with bookings, payments and loyalty_cards to derive per-client booking counts, lifetime spend and first/last booking dates, then segments every client as New (0-1 bookings) or Returning (2+) with search and filter tabs. Not standalone - it calls requireRole('admin') on line 6 and relies on index.php having already loaded config.php/functions.php and defined $user.
nodes.languageNotes: Procedural page rendered as inline HTML after a closing `?>`; results are loaded in a single pass with no LIMIT/OFFSET, so the page size grows linearly with the client count.

nodes.name: dashboard.php
nodes.summary: Admin sales-and-analytics dashboard, the largest page in the project: computes revenue vs. booked sales, pending approvals, walk-in vs online split, a dynamic (capped at 24 months) monthly sales and booking trend, top-5 packages by revenue, per-package sales, busiest weekday analysis and a low-stock alert list. Roughly two thirds of its 2350 lines are inline CSS and HTML rather than PHP logic.
nodes.languageNotes: Only lines 1-323 are PHP; lines 325-1180 are an inlined <style> block and the file emits its own <!DOCTYPE html>/<head>/<body>, so when index.php requires it the page renders a nested HTML document inside the shared header/sidebar/footer layout. Charts are pure PHP-computed CSS bars - no JavaScript charting library and no fetch() calls.

nodes.name: feedback.php
nodes.summary: Admin feedback console handling delete, resolve, mark-urgent, AI re-analyze and send-reply POST actions (all CSRF-verified), calling analyzeFeedbackWithAI() from ai_helper.php and falling back to a local Tagalog/English keyword sentiment scorer when the AI columns are absent. Renders filterable review stats plus a sentiment-prioritized urgent list.
nodes.languageNotes: Probes the schema at runtime with SHOW COLUMNS FROM feedback LIKE 'ai_sentiment' / 'topics' / 'reply_sentat' style checks and degrades gracefully, so it works on installs that predate the AI and reply columns. Sending a reply both inserts a client notification (addNotification) and stamps reply_sent_at/replied_by.

nodes.name: getSegmentInfo
nodes.summary: Maps a segment name to the badge class, emoji icon, colour palette and human description used to render the New vs Returning client cards.

nodes.name: getTopicIcon
nodes.summary: Maps an AI-classified feedback topic (photographer, delivery, pricing, studio, staff, ...) to an emoji glyph, defaulting to a speech bubble.

nodes.name: getTopicLabel
nodes.summary: Returns the human-readable label for a feedback topic, falling back to ucfirst() of the raw topic value when it is not in the known set.

nodes.name: getTopicColor
nodes.summary: Returns the hex accent colour assigned to a feedback topic for badge, chip and border styling.

nodes.name: analyzeSentimentLocal
nodes.summary: Offline sentiment classifier that counts Tagalog and English positive/negative keyword hits in a comment, biases the score by star rating, and returns positive/negative/neutral when Gemini results are unavailable.

nodes.name: inventory.php
nodes.summary: Inventory CRUD page open to both admin and staff: adds items, updates quantities in place, and refuses deletion when an item is still referenced by booking_inventory rows. Every mutation calls checkLowStockAndNotify() so alerts fire immediately, and the listing annotates each item with an in-use count derived from unreturned booking_inventory records.
nodes.languageNotes: Like dashboard.php it emits a complete HTML document (lines 80-718) with its own inlined stylesheet, producing a nested document inside the router layout. The threshold logic is duplicated between the $lowItems filter on line 76 and the low-stock query in dashboard.php.

nodes.name: loyalty-cards.php
nodes.summary: Read-only admin view of the loyalty program: joins users to loyalty_cards, attaches a tier through getLoyaltyTier(), filters by the corrected 2/4/7/10 booking thresholds, and shows tier badges plus progress toward the next reward. Performs no writes and is not exposed to client or staff navigation.
nodes.languageNotes: The tier thresholds are hardcoded twice more than ideal - in the inline filters (lines 43-55) and inside getLoyaltyBadge()/getProgressToNextTier() - and must be kept in sync with getLoyaltyTier()/getLoyaltyRewards() in functions.php; the PACKAGES and LOYALTY_TIERS constants in config.php are dead code and do not drive this page.

nodes.name: getLoyaltyBadge
nodes.summary: Returns the inline-styled reward badge markup for a client based on total bookings (2+ extra minutes, 4+ extra print, 7+ extra backdrop, 10+ 50% off).

nodes.name: getProgressToNextTier
nodes.summary: Computes the percentage of progress from the client's current tier toward the next one and returns the next reward label and booking threshold, including a max-tier case.

nodes.name: notifications.php
nodes.summary: Shared notification inbox for admin, staff and clients: opens a notification (marking it read and redirecting to its internal link), marks all as read, deletes single entries, and renders the latest 100 notifications styled per type. Every branch prefers the functions.php helper (getNotifications, markNotificationRead, markAllNotificationsRead, deleteNotification) and falls back to equivalent inline SQL.
nodes.languageNotes: Unlike its sibling admin pages it does not call requireRole() - it uses a conditional requireLogin() and resolves the identity via `$user ?? currentUser()`, bailing out with an inline error block when no user id is available. isSafeNotificationLink() only accepts relative index.php?page=... targets, guarding stored notification links against open redirects. Push delivery (sendPushNotification in functions.php) silently no-ops because Minishlink\WebPush is absent from vendor/.

nodes.name: isSafeNotificationLink
nodes.summary: Validates a notification's stored link, permitting only relative internal index.php?page=... targets and rejecting absolute URLs, protocol-relative links and javascript: style values before redirecting.

nodes.name: formatNotificationDate
nodes.summary: Formats a notification timestamp as 'M d, Y - h:i A', returning the raw string untouched when the value cannot be parsed.

nodes.name: getNotificationIcon
nodes.summary: Chooses the emoji shown for a notification, preferring the stored icon column and otherwise deriving one from the notification type (booking, payment, inventory, feedback, urgent_feedback, new_client, photo, system).

nodes.name: getNotificationTypeClass
nodes.summary: Maps a notification type to the CSS class (type-booking, type-payment, type-inventory, type-feedback, type-client, type-photo, type-system) consumed by the page's inlined stylesheet.

nodes.name: packages.php
nodes.summary: Admin CRUD page over the packages table: creates and updates packages with an image upload, soft-deletes them by setting is_active=0, and renders main packages with their sub-packages grouped through parent_id. Images are stored under assets/packages/ with a validated MIME type and a random filename.
nodes.languageNotes: Upload validation is content-based (finfo MIME sniff rather than the client-supplied Content-Type), capped at 5MB, with pkg_<timestamp>_<random hex> filenames; replacing or removing an image unlinks the old file. Delete is a soft delete - the row stays but is_active=0, while child sub-packages are only detached client-side.

nodes.name: handleImageUpload
nodes.summary: Validates and stores an uploaded package image: 5MB size cap, finfo MIME allow-list for JPEG/PNG/GIF/WebP, randomized filename under assets/packages/, and a flash message on any failure path.

nodes.name: payments.php
nodes.summary: Admin payment ledger: aggregates total revenue, pending, refunded and unpaid-reservation figures from the payments and bookings tables, then lists transactions joined to clients, bookings, packages and the users who refunded or verified them, with a status filter and derived on-site vs walk-in source labels.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines a local RESERVATION_FEE = 100 constant and interpolates it straight into SQL (safe because it is a literal, unlike the bound parameters); the unpaid-reservation total is derived as fee x unpaid bookings rather than read from stored deposits, so it can drift from actual payment records. Mutating payment actions live in pages/api/record-payment.php, not here.

nodes.name: profile.php
nodes.summary: Shared profile page for any logged-in user: dispatches POST actions to edit name/email/phone, change the password, and upload an avatar, then renders the profile UI in the same file. It is rendered by index.php and depends on the router having already defined $user and $role -- its only guard is an isset() check that redirects to login.php.
nodes.languageNotes: State-changing POST handlers here run with no csrfField()/verifyCsrf() pair, unlike staff.php and settings.php in the same directory. Avatars are MIME-sniffed with finfo and capped at 2MB.

nodes.name: reports.php
nodes.summary: Admin-only reports and analytics module exposing 9 report types (inventory, appointment, payment, sales, loyalty, analytics, evaluation, chatbot, photos) with on-screen tables plus PDF and CSV export. Revenue is derived from actual paid payments rather than booking totals, and the analytics report computes genuine period-over-period deltas instead of hard-coded percentages.
nodes.languageNotes: Helpers are wrapped in if (!function_exists(...)) guards and the FPDF subclass sits inside a runtime if ($fpdfLoaded) block, so conditional declarations are invisible to static parsers. FPDF itself is hand-vendored under includes/fpdf/, not installed via Composer.

nodes.name: sales.php
nodes.summary: Admin sales ledger that filters the payments table by date range, status, payment method and free-text search, then derives summary cards plus daily-revenue, per-package and per-method breakdowns for charting. The transaction query, metric aggregates and chart queries all reuse the same WHERE clause so the summary cards always match the table below them.

nodes.name: settings.php
nodes.summary: Admin-only settings screen that persists studio identity, opening hours and GCash/Maribank account details into the settings key/value table and handles QR-code image uploads. Every text field is written with INSERT ... ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, and each QR upload is MIME-sniffed, capped at 5MB and has its predecessor file deleted.
nodes.languageNotes: Uploads land in uploads/payment/ rather than the UPLOAD_DIR constant (assets/uploads/), one of the six scattered upload roots in this project.

nodes.name: staff.php
nodes.summary: Admin page for managing staff accounts: adds a user with the staff role, flips is_active, and deletes staff rows via a CSRF-checked POST handler that redirects back to index.php?page=staff. The listing pulls every staff user together with a count of the bookings each one managed.

nodes.name: chatbot-ai.php
nodes.summary: Standalone SnapBot AI JSON endpoint for the public booking site that runs a three-stage cascade: live availability answered from the bookings table, then a hard-coded Studio 94 FAQ, then a Gemini generateContent call across a four-model fallback chain. Every reply is persisted to chat_history and markdown is stripped before the JSON response is emitted.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on a POST endpoint with no authentication, and hard-codes prices, hours and policies into the Gemini system prompt instead of reading the packages/settings tables -- so the chatbot and the database can disagree.

nodes.name: check-client-loyalty.php
nodes.summary: Standalone staff/admin JSON endpoint that resolves a client by phone or email and returns their loyalty booking count, bonus minutes, discount percentage and tier label for the booking form. The tier thresholds are duplicated inline rather than delegated to getLoyaltyTier() in functions.php, so the two definitions can drift apart.
nodes.languageNotes: Returns the raw $e->getMessage() text in the JSON error payload, which leaks database error detail to the caller.

nodes.name: check_availability.php
nodes.summary: Standalone staff/admin JSON endpoint that builds a 15-minute slot grid between 10:00 AM and 7:00 PM for a given date and package, adding a capped loyalty bonus to the package duration. Slots carry a three-state result -- available, pending approval, or fully booked -- with confirmed bookings taking priority over awaiting-approval ones.
nodes.languageNotes: Package length is recovered from a free-text duration column by regex (extractMinutesFromDuration) rather than stored as minutes, so an unfamiliar duration string silently falls back to 60.

nodes.name: getReportData
nodes.summary: Single 700-line switch that runs the SQL for each of the 9 report types and returns the row set plus per-report flags. The analytics branch additionally loads the equivalent previous period so real change percentages can be computed.

nodes.name: generateReportPDF
nodes.summary: Renders any of the 9 reports into a paginated PDF via the Studio94ReportPDF subclass, with per-report column widths, a filled table header, type-specific row formatting and alternating row shading.

nodes.name: reportStatusBadge
nodes.summary: Maps a status string onto the green/amber/red/gray badge classes used across every report table, covering payment, booking, inventory and equipment condition vocabularies.

nodes.name: reportDate
nodes.summary: Formats a database date as 'Mon DD, YYYY', rendering an em dash for empty values and falling back to the escaped raw string when it cannot be parsed.

nodes.name: validReportDate
nodes.summary: Strict Y-m-d validator built on DateTime::createFromFormat with a round-trip format comparison, used to reject tampered from/to query parameters before they reach SQL.

nodes.name: Studio94ReportPDF
nodes.summary: FPDF subclass that transcodes UTF-8 text to windows-1252 with //TRANSLIT//IGNORE before writing cells, which is what lets peso signs and accented characters survive PDF export. Declared conditionally inside if ($fpdfLoaded).

nodes.name: salesStatusClass
nodes.summary: Returns the success/warning/danger/neutral CSS class for a payment status, bucketing PAID/VERIFIED/COMPLETED as green and REJECTED/FAILED/CANCELLED as red.

nodes.name: salesStatusLabel
nodes.summary: Maps a payment status onto an emoji-prefixed human label such as 'AWAITING PAYMENT', passing unknown statuses through unchanged instead of hiding them.

nodes.name: handleQrUpload
nodes.summary: Validates a GCash/Maribank QR upload via finfo MIME sniffing, writes it to uploads/payment/ with a random-suffixed filename, upserts the stored path into settings, and unlinks the replaced file.

nodes.name: cleanBotText
nodes.summary: Strips code fences, bold/italic markers and backticks from a Gemini reply, converts markdown bullets to the bullet character, collapses runs of blank lines and trims per-line whitespace so the text is safe to inject into the chat widget.

nodes.name: saveChatLog
nodes.summary: Inserts the user message and bot reply into chat_history, falling back to user id 1 for anonymous visitors and swallowing any database error to error_log so logging can never break a chat reply.

nodes.name: isAvailabilityQuestion
nodes.summary: Regex gate that decides whether a normalized user message is asking about booking availability, checking English and Filipino/Tagalog phrasings ('may slot ba', 'available ba sa') so the chatbot answers from the database instead of hallucinating.

nodes.name: parseRequestedDate
nodes.summary: Resolves a requested date from natural language -- today/tomorrow, weekday names, explicit month-day or ISO dates, and plain 'the 26th' -- returning a Manila-timezone DateTime or null to trigger a clarifying prompt.

nodes.name: parseRequestedTime
nodes.summary: Extracts an optional requested start time such as '2pm' or '14:00' from the user message so the availability answer can focus on that slot.

nodes.name: getBookingsForDate
nodes.summary: Loads all non-cancelled, non-rejected bookings for a date joined to their package duration, returning normalised start/end minute intervals used for overlap checks.

nodes.name: mergeSlots
nodes.summary: Collapses overlapping or contiguous free intervals into a minimal set of bookable windows so the chatbot reports genuinely open stretches rather than a slot-by-slot list.

nodes.name: buildAvailabilityResponse
nodes.summary: Turns a date plus its bookings into the conversational English answer, reporting free windows, flagging dates that are fully booked and calling out when every remaining slot is still awaiting approval.

nodes.name: answerFAQ
nodes.summary: Regex-matched FAQ covering packages, prices, hours, location, GCash payment and the non-refundable cancellation policy, returning null when nothing matches so the request falls through to the Gemini fallback.

nodes.name: callGemini
nodes.summary: Posts a system-instruction-separated payload to the Gemini generateContent endpoint via cURL, iterating the model fallback chain, logging each failure and surfacing the finish_reason so truncated answers can be detected. Disables SSL peer verification, which is a real MITM risk for an API carrying the Gemini key.

nodes.name: check_new_notifications.php
nodes.summary: Standalone JSON polling endpoint backing the client's notification bell: with ?all=1 it returns the total unread count for the badge, otherwise with ?since=<unix_ts> it returns up to five unread notifications created since that timestamp. Self-requires config.php and functions.php, does its own isLoggedIn() plus role allow-list check, and degrades to a success:false JSON body rather than a non-200 code when the database is unreachable.
nodes.languageNotes: Sets no-cache headers explicitly because assets/js/app.js polls this endpoint on a timer; every failure branch echoes JSON and exits rather than throwing.

nodes.name: client-payments.php
nodes.summary: Client-scoped JSON API with three actions selected by ?action=: 'settings' returns the GCash and Maribank account/QR details from the settings table, 'list' returns the client's payment rows joined to bookings and packages plus computed totals, and 'submit' accepts a CSRF-protected payment-proof screenshot upload. Uploads are extension- and size-validated (5 MB, images only) and written to assets/uploads/payments/ rather than the UPLOAD_DIR constant.
nodes.languageNotes: Hard-codes the 100 peso RESERVATION_FEE as a local variable and duplicates the loyalty-discount thresholds that getLoyaltyTier() implements elsewhere; extensive error_log() debug tracing is still present in the submit path.

nodes.name: get-day-bookings.php
nodes.summary: Zero-byte placeholder file with no PHP, no requires, and no consumers. It is a dead stub: any request to it returns an empty 200 response, and nothing in the codebase references it.
nodes.languageNotes: Because the file is empty it fails silently rather than erroring, so it is easy to mistake for a working endpoint in traces.

nodes.name: inventory-usage.php
nodes.summary: Read-only JSON endpoint that returns up to 50 rows of usage history for a single inventory item by joining booking_inventory to bookings, restricted to admin and staff. Takes the item id from ?id= and returns { success, usage, count } with no-store of state.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards with isLoggedIn() plus an in_array role check rather than the requireRole() helper used elsewhere in pages/api/.

nodes.name: record-payment.php
nodes.summary: Staff/admin JSON endpoint for recording on-site payments, accepting both raw JSON bodies and multipart FormData so an optional proof image can accompany the payment. Handles RESERVATION (flat 100 peso), BALANCE, and FULL types, applies the 10-booking 50% loyalty discount, then writes the payment row and flips the booking status to Deposit Paid or Confirmed inside one transaction before firing client and admin notifications.
nodes.languageNotes: Guarded by requireLogin() + requireRole(['staff','admin']); the loyalty discount is recomputed from loyalty_cards.total_bookings here rather than reusing getLoyaltyTier(), so the threshold is duplicated across the codebase. Catch block calls rollBack() before echoing a 500 body.

nodes.name: booking.php
nodes.summary: Client booking-creation page reached through the index.php router (index.php?page=booking); it calls requireRole('client') at line 2 with no require_once of its own, so it is not standalone and would fatal if opened directly. The POST handler validates package, date, time, headcount against the studio's 10:00-19:00 window, and detects schedule overlaps before inserting the booking, an UNPAID RESERVATION payment row, and a loyalty card increment, then fires a staff notification. Roughly the last 800 lines are a large inline <script> block implementing the calendar, slot grid, and sub-package drill-down.
nodes.languageNotes: Defines extractHoursFromDuration(), extractMinutesFromDuration(), and checkBookingConflict() inside if (!function_exists(...)) guards; functions.php already defines checkBookingConflict() at line 1232, so the local copy at line 45 is a never-executed fallback on the normal router path. Page-specific CSS is inlined in a <style> block rather than assets/css/styles.css, and the inline JavaScript re-implements the same duration parser in JavaScript for client-side slot checks.

nodes.name: extractHoursFromDuration
nodes.summary: Parses a free-text package duration string such as '2 hours 30 MIN' or 'Half Day' into a float hour count, falling back to 1.0 hour for empty input. Handles named half/whole-day variants before falling back to regex extraction of numeric hour and minute components.
nodes.languageNotes: Wrapped in an if (!function_exists()) guard because functions.php provides the same-named helper.

nodes.name: extractMinutesFromDuration
nodes.summary: One-line adapter that converts a package duration string into whole minutes by multiplying the parsed hour count by 60 and rounding.

nodes.name: checkBookingConflict
nodes.summary: Detects overlapping bookings for a given date and time by loading every active booking joined to its package and doing interval-overlap arithmetic on start/end timestamps. Falls back to the package duration when duration_minutes is null and additionally scrapes a '+N MIN bonus applied' loyalty note out of the free-text notes field to extend the occupied window.
nodes.languageNotes: Duplicated from functions.php:1232 behind a function_exists guard, so only one definition is ever live; the loyalty bonus is encoded as text inside notes and re-parsed with a regex here.

nodes.name: getAvailableSlots
nodes.summary: Client-side counterpart of checkBookingConflict that filters the server-rendered booked-slot list down to start times that fit the selected package duration inside the studio's opening hours without overlapping an existing booking.
nodes.languageNotes: JavaScript, not PHP: it mirrors the PHP conflict logic above inside the page's inline <script> block, so availability rules are duplicated across the server and client.

nodes.name: updateBookedSlotsDisplay
nodes.summary: Re-renders the time-slot grid for a chosen date, marking each slot as available, booked, pending, or confirmed and wiring up click handlers plus the booked/available counters. This is the main state-refresh path when the user changes date or package.

nodes.name: checkTimeAvailability
nodes.summary: Runs the full client-side validation of a chosen start time for the selected package: parsing the time, enforcing the 10 AM-7 PM studio window and end-before-close rule, checking headcount against the package maximum, and probing availability against existing bookings.
nodes.languageNotes: Largest single function in the page; repeats the same 10:00/19:00 boundaries as the OPEN_HOUR_MINUTES and CLOSE_HOUR_MINUTES constants defined at the top of the PHP block, so the two can drift.

nodes.name: renderCalendar
nodes.summary: Builds the month calendar grid for the selected view month, marks days that are past, today, fully booked, or available, and attaches the date-selection handlers that drive the slot grid below it.

nodes.name: bookings.php
nodes.summary: Client booking-list page rendered via index.php?page=bookings; like the other pages/<role>/ files it opens with requireRole('client') and has no require_once of its own. Handles the POST cancel action (blocked within one day of the shoot and on terminal statuses, cascades the cancellation to UNPAID/PENDING payment rows and notifies admin and staff), then renders every booking joined to its package, parent package, and reservation payment with per-status counts.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses the classic header('Location: ...') post-redirect-get pattern rather than APP_URL-aware redirects, and hardcodes RESERVATION_FEE as a const that duplicates the value in pages/client/booking.php and pages/api/record-payment.php.

nodes.name: bookingStatusBadge
nodes.summary: Maps a booking status string to its CSS badge class and emoji label, returning a neutral grey badge for unmapped values. Escapes only the fallback branch of the status text.

nodes.name: dashboard.php
nodes.summary: Client landing page served at index.php?page=dashboard; begins with requireRole('client') and depends on index.php having already loaded config.php and functions.php and defined $user. Assembles the loyalty card summary, the next upcoming session, five recent bookings, three recently delivered photos, and a dynamic 'Welcome back' vs 'Welcome' greeting, then renders it with a page-scoped inline <style> block.
nodes.languageNotes: Reads loyalty progress through getLoyaltyRewards() and getLoyaltyProgress() but redefines the tier labels (2/4/7/10) in a local $tiers array rather than reusing getLoyaltyTier(), duplicating the thresholds.

nodes.name: feedback.php
nodes.summary: Client feedback page where a customer submits a review for a completed booking, with Gemini AI sentiment analysis (local keyword/regex fallback), automatic topic tagging, urgent-escalation notifications, and a filterable review history grouped by service type. Not a standalone script: it opens with requireRole('client') and assumes index.php already loaded config.php/functions.php and defined $user, $role and $page.
nodes.languageNotes: Procedural PHP template with ~500 lines of inline <style> and ~95 lines of inline <script>. The INSERT into feedback is rebuilt across four branches based on SHOW COLUMNS probing for the optional ai_sentiment / booking_id / topics columns, so the page degrades gracefully on older schemas.

nodes.name: analyzeSentimentLocal
nodes.summary: Keyword-scoring sentiment fallback that counts Filipino and English positive/negative terms in a comment and returns 'positive', 'negative' or 'neutral'. Used when analyzeFeedbackWithAI() from ai_helper.php is unavailable or throws.

nodes.name: detectTopicsLocal
nodes.summary: Regex topic detector that tags a comment with any of seven categories (photographer, quality, print, staff, delivery, pricing, studio) and defaults to 'general' when nothing matches. Result is stored as a comma-separated string in feedback.topics.

nodes.name: classifyFeedbackByService
nodes.summary: Maps a package name to one of five service buckets (self-shoot, creative, family, studio-rental, other) via chained strpos checks, returning a key, display label, emoji icon and theme colour used for service badges and the filter counters.

nodes.name: getTopicIcon
nodes.summary: Dictionary lookup returning the emoji icon for a detected feedback topic, falling back to a speech bubble for unknown values.

nodes.name: getTopicLabel
nodes.summary: Returns the human-readable label for a feedback topic, falling back to a ucfirst() of the raw topic string when the topic is not in the map.

nodes.name: getTopicColor
nodes.summary: Returns the hex theme colour for a feedback topic, used to style the topic tag pills in the rendered review list.

nodes.name: notifications.php
nodes.summary: Client notification inbox that handles mark-all-read, single-read, single-delete and delete-all-read through GET parameters, then queries the notifications table filtered by all/unread/read and renders the list with an unread badge. Not a standalone script: it opens with requireRole('client') and depends on index.php having already loaded config.php and functions.php and defined $user.
nodes.languageNotes: State changes are done with GET redirects rather than CSRF-protected POSTs; the per-user ownership check is enforced in the WHERE clause instead (id AND user_id).

nodes.name: payments.php
nodes.summary: Client 'My Payments' page that is ~99% inline CSS plus a large vanilla-JS single-page app: it fetches settings and grouped payment lists from pages/api/client-payments.php, renders GCash and Maribank QR codes, handles deposit vs. remaining-balance payment submission, and applies the 10-booking loyalty discount. The only PHP logic is the requireRole('client') auth gate.
nodes.languageNotes: Duplicates server-side rendering helpers (fmtMoney, esc, statusBadgeJS, formatDateJS) in JavaScript; all data access is delegated to the pages/api/client-payments.php JSON endpoint rather than inline PHP queries.

nodes.name: photos.php
nodes.summary: Client photo-gallery page that lists the user's Completed bookings joined to packages with a photo count and latest upload date, then lazily loads a per-session thumbnail grid on demand. Read-only: it issues no writes and relies on the router having loaded config.php and functions.php.

nodes.name: profile.php
nodes.summary: User profile page (header comment marks it 'Shared') that processes three POST actions - update_profile, change_password and upload_avatar - re-reads the user row afterwards, and renders the profile form and avatar. Unlike the other pages in this batch it does not call requireRole(); it falls back to redirecting to login.php when $user or $role is unset, so it serves as the pages/<page>.php fallback when a role-specific profile page is missing.
nodes.languageNotes: Avatar uploads are written to a pages-scoped uploads directory rather than the UPLOAD_DIR constant defined in config.php.

nodes.name: bookings.php
nodes.summary: Admin/staff bookings management page covering the full booking lifecycle: CSRF-verified approve/complete/cancel transitions that trigger notifications and inventory deduction on completion, walk-in booking creation with checkBookingConflict() and automatic loyalty-card enrollment, plus an on-site payment modal recording deposit or remaining balance. Models a fixed 100-peso reservation fee and shows loyalty milestones (2/4/7/10 bookings).
nodes.languageNotes: Declares a file-level const RESERVATION_FEE = 100 inside the included page scope and computes a 50% loyalty discount inline in the template rather than through getLoyaltyRewards() in functions.php.

nodes.name: clients.php
nodes.summary: Staff client directory supporting a name/email LIKE search that aggregates each client's total booking count, total PAID spend and most recent booking date via LEFT JOINs against bookings and payments. Pure read-only listing page with no POST handling.
nodes.languageNotes: The LIKE clause is conditionally concatenated into the SQL string and the parameter array is built alongside it, since prepared statements cannot bind an identifier.

nodes.name: dashboard.php
nodes.summary: Admin/staff landing dashboard that aggregates booking status counts, same-day conflict detection, pending approvals, confirmed-today bookings, upcoming bookings, today's full schedule and today's walk-ins, then renders them as stat cards and lists. Chooses a 'Welcome back' vs 'Hello' greeting from the session login_count.
nodes.languageNotes: Issues seven separate unparameterized COUNT/SELECT queries per request instead of one aggregate pass; the conflicting-package logic duplicates the domain rule that checkBookingConflict() implements in functions.php.

nodes.name: feedback.php
nodes.summary: Staff feedback console that lists all client reviews joined to users, normalizes sentiment per row (preferring the stored ai_sentiment column and falling back to a local keyword analyzer), flags urgent items, and lets staff store a reply that fires addNotification() to the client. The only page in this batch that explicitly require_once's ai_helper.php, and the only one that declares PHP functions.
nodes.languageNotes: Probes the schema at runtime with SHOW COLUMNS FROM feedback LIKE ... for ai_sentiment, topics and reply_sent_at, wrapping each in try/catch and degrading to the local analyzer when a column is missing - the same ALTER-at-runtime tolerance as ensureDatabaseSchema().

nodes.name: getTopicIcon
nodes.summary: Maps a normalized feedback topic string to an emoji icon used in the review list.

nodes.name: getTopicLabel
nodes.summary: Converts a feedback topic slug into a trimmed, capitalized human-readable label.

nodes.name: getTopicColor
nodes.summary: Returns the accent color associated with a feedback topic for consistent theming across the review cards.

nodes.name: analyzeSentimentLocal
nodes.summary: Offline fallback sentiment classifier: substring-counts Tagalog and English positive/negative keyword lists in the comment and weights the numeric rating (+/-2 at 4+ and 2-), returning positive, negative or neutral. Used whenever the Gemini-backed ai_sentiment column is absent or empty.
nodes.languageNotes: Purely lexical substring matching (strpos), so no tokenizer or external service is required - it works with the Gemini integration completely unavailable.

nodes.name: getSentimentBadge
nodes.summary: Maps a sentiment value to its CSS badge class using a PHP match expression (green/red/purple, amber default).
nodes.languageNotes: Uses PHP 8 match(true-style) expression semantics with a default arm, so unknown or null sentiment values fall back safely.

nodes.name: getSentimentIcon
nodes.summary: Returns the emoji glyph corresponding to a sentiment value (positive, negative, mixed, neutral).

nodes.name: getSentimentLabel
nodes.summary: Returns the capitalized display text for a sentiment value.

nodes.name: getSentimentInlineStyle
nodes.summary: Returns an inline CSS declaration overriding the badge colors, applied only to the 'mixed' sentiment; returns an empty string otherwise.

nodes.name: isUrgentFeedback
nodes.summary: Business rule that flags a review for staff escalation: honours an explicit is_urgent flag, or infers urgency from a negative sentiment, or from mixed sentiment combined with an overall rating of 3 or below.

nodes.name: inventory.php
nodes.summary: Staff/admin inventory management page for the `inventory` table: CSRF-protected add / update_quantity / delete actions (delete is blocked when `booking_inventory` references the item), a red low-stock alert banner computed inline from non-reusable items at or below threshold, and an inline JS edit modal. Not standalone — it opens with requireRole(['admin','staff']) and relies on index.php having already loaded config.php/functions.php and defined $user/$role.
nodes.languageNotes: Laravel-style Blade echo (`<?= ?>`) and inline CSS/JS are embedded directly in the PHP template; every mutating branch calls setFlash() then header('Location: index.php?page=inventory') and exit (POST-redirect-GET).

nodes.name: notifications.php
nodes.summary: Small staff-only notification inbox that lists the last 50 `notifications` rows for the current user with all/unread/read filters, plus a `?markread=1` GET action that flips every row to is_read=1. Only 49 lines of which most is HTML; relies on the router having loaded config.php/functions.php and set $user.

nodes.name: payments.php
nodes.summary: Payment verification console for staff/admin: handles verify / reject / refund POST actions, recomputing effective price from `loyalty_cards.total_bookings` (50% off at 10+ bookings), flipping `bookings` to Deposit Paid / Confirmed, and notifying the client via addNotification(). Adds a filter+search list query over payments joined to bookings, packages, users and loyalty_cards with status-ordered counts, then renders a list view whose rows open detail / proof / reject / refund modals.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares `const RESERVATION_FEE = 100;` at file scope — a redeclaration hazard if the page were ever included twice in one request.

nodes.name: profile.php
nodes.summary: Shared self-service profile page for staff/admin (identical copy also served under pages/client) handling three POST actions — update_profile (with email uniqueness check and session resync), change_password (current-password verify + password_hash), and upload_avatar (finfo MIME sniffing, 2MB cap, writes to assets/uploads/avatars/ and unlinks the old file). Notably it does NOT call requireRole(); it only guards on `isset($user)`/`isset($role)` and redirects to login.php, and it calls db() seven separate times instead of reusing one handle.
nodes.languageNotes: No csrfField()/verifyCsrf() on any of the three forms, unlike the other pages in this batch — CSRF protection is inconsistent across the codebase.

nodes.name: schedule.php
nodes.summary: Read-only staff schedule board that groups non-cancelled bookings by date and splits each day into online vs walk-in buckets (detected from booking type or a 'WALK' booking_ref prefix), with upcoming / today / tomorrow / week views driven by a CURDATE()-based WHERE builder. No POST handling and no CSRF surface.

nodes.name: upload.php
nodes.summary: Staff photo-delivery page: CSRF-protected multi-file upload that filters extensions (jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/raw), caps each file at 50MB, writes into UPLOAD_DIR (assets/uploads/), inserts a `photos` row per file, and notifies the client via addNotification() once at least one file lands. Also lists Completed/Deposit Paid sessions eligible for upload and a 10-row upload history.
nodes.languageNotes: Writes to the UPLOAD_DIR constant (assets/uploads/) rather than pages/upload/payments/ — upload destinations in this project are scattered across several directories.

nodes.name: walkin.php
nodes.summary: The largest page in the batch: a walk-in booking flow that ALTERs `bookings` to add duration_minutes at request time, parses package duration strings into minutes, detects schedule conflicts, finds-or-creates the client user (issuing a random password sent via addNotification), inserts the walk-in booking plus a Pending RESERVATION payment row, bumps loyalty_cards, and notifies admin+staff. Ships ~500 lines of inline JS for package drill-down, a month calendar with availability colouring, quick-time dropdown, and an async loyalty lookup against pages/api/check-client-loyalty.php.
nodes.languageNotes: Wraps every helper in `if (!function_exists(...))` because this page is reachable through more than one include path; also probes for the duration_minutes column and keeps two INSERT variants so the page survives a partially-migrated database.

nodes.name: service-workers.js
nodes.summary: Web Push service worker that displays notifications from a JSON push payload with vibrate/sound/action buttons and opens /index.php?page=notifications on click; the fetch handler is network-first with an 'Offline' 503 fallback. Dead in practice — no `navigator.serviceWorker.register()` call exists anywhere in the project, so this file is never installed.
nodes.languageNotes: Declares CACHE_NAME = 'notifications-v1' but never calls caches.open(), so the cache is unused vestigial config.

nodes.name: parsePackageDurationToMinutes
nodes.summary: Normalizes the free-text `packages.duration` column into integer minutes, handling half-day (240), whole-day (480), 'N-M hour', 'N-M min', compound 'Nh Mm', decimal hours, bare minutes, and a bare-number fallback of 60.

nodes.name: resolveBookingDurationMinutes
nodes.summary: Returns a booking's effective length in minutes, preferring the stored duration_minutes column and otherwise falling back to parsePackageDurationToMinutes() plus any '+N MIN bonus applied' marker smuggled into the booking notes.
nodes.languageNotes: The loyalty bonus is persisted by appending a human-readable line to bookings.notes, so conflict logic has to regex the notes column to reconstruct real durations.

nodes.name: parseTimeToMinutes
nodes.summary: Parses a 'h:mm AM/PM' time string into minutes-since-midnight, handling the 12 AM/PM edge cases, and returns null on any unparsable input so callers can surface a validation error.

nodes.name: calculateWalkinLoyaltyBonus
nodes.summary: Duplicates the loyalty thresholds inline — 1+ prior bookings grants a 5-minute bonus, 10+ grants a 50% discount — returning bonus_minutes / discount_pct / has_loyalty / has_discount for the walk-in booking path.
nodes.languageNotes: These 1/10 thresholds are copy-pasted from getLoyaltyTier()/getLoyaltyRewards() in functions.php rather than calling them, so the two copies can drift.

nodes.name: checkWalkinConflict
nodes.summary: Server-side double-booking guard: loads every blocking booking for the given date (Confirmed / In Progress / Completed / Deposit Paid / Approved (Unpaid)), reconstructs each one's duration via resolveBookingDurationMinutes(), and returns true if the proposed interval overlaps any of them.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses classic interval-overlap math (newStart < exEnd && newEnd > exStart) and branches its SELECT list on the runtime-probed $hasDurationColumn global.

nodes.name: send-verification.php
nodes.summary: Transactional email helper library required by login.php that delivers account-verification and password-reset messages. Tries the Resend REST API over HTTPS 443 first and falls back to PHPMailer SMTP, because outbound SMTP ports are blocked on Railway.
nodes.languageNotes: Requires config.php then vendor/autoload.php; lives outside the index.php router and exposes only global functions plus inline HTML email templates as heredoc strings.

nodes.name: isMailConfigured
nodes.summary: Returns true when either a RESEND_API_KEY constant or non-empty MAIL_USERNAME/MAIL_PASSWORD constants are available, gating all outbound mail.

nodes.name: sendViaResend
nodes.summary: Posts a JSON payload to the Resend HTTPS API with raw cURL and reports delivery via the HTTP status code, logging both success and failure paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses raw curl_init/curl_setopt rather than a client library, with CURLOPT_RETURNTRANSFER and an explicit 200/201 status check.

nodes.name: sendViaPhpMailer
nodes.summary: Fallback SMTP delivery path that configures PHPMailer for Gmail, retries once with a second SMTP instance, and returns false on any exception.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains a duplicated retry block using a $mail2 instance, an unusual near-copy-paste pattern for a second delivery attempt.

nodes.name: sendVerificationEmail
nodes.summary: Builds the branded HTML/plain-text verification email containing an APP_URL/verify.php link and dispatches it through Resend then PHPMailer, returning 'sent', 'skipped', or 'failed'.

nodes.name: sendPasswordResetEmail
nodes.summary: Sends the password-reset email using the same Resend-then-SMTP dispatch chain as verification, returning a plain boolean result.

nodes.name: sidebar.php
nodes.summary: Role-aware navigation sidebar rendered on every authenticated page. Hardcodes the $navAdmin/$navStaff/$navClient link tables that must stay in sync with the $rolePages allowlist in index.php, resolves the avatar path, counts unread notifications, and embeds its own inline CSS and JavaScript.
nodes.languageNotes: Has no require statements — it is included by index.php after $role, $page and $user are defined, so it calls clean(), db(), getUnreadCount() and the APP_URL constant from that shared context rather than loading them itself.

nodes.name: hash.php
nodes.summary: Nine-line throwaway developer utility that prints a password_hash() value plus a ready-to-run UPDATE statement resetting the password of every seeded demo account. Not part of the application and referenced by nothing.

nodes.name: install.php
nodes.summary: Browser-accessible database installer that loads config.php and functions.php, detects whether the users table already exists, then strips CREATE DATABASE/USE statements from install.sql and executes the whole file in one PDO call. Ships with no authentication of any kind, so it must be removed or locked down before any production deploy.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses $pdo->exec() on the raw multi-statement SQL text; POST and ?run=1 both trigger execution, and force_install=1 is the only guard against clobbering an existing database.

nodes.name: install.sql
nodes.summary: Complete bootstrap schema for SnapTrack: eleven CREATE TABLE statements followed by seed data for settings, users, packages, sub-packages, inventory, bookings, payments, feedback, notifications and loyalty cards. Comments are in Filipino, and ensureDatabaseSchema() in functions.php must be kept in sync with any column added here.
nodes.languageNotes: Every statement is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so the script is idempotent, but the CREATE DATABASE and USE lines are commented out and stripped at runtime by install.php.

nodes.name: users
nodes.summary: Account table covering credentials, role and active state, lockout tracking, email verification tokens, Google OAuth linkage, TOTP MFA secrets and backup codes, and an optional parent_id for family sub-accounts.

nodes.name: packages
nodes.summary: Studio package catalogue with a self-referencing parent_id that models sub-packages under a main package, plus price, duration, features JSON, theme colour, popularity flag and max_pax.

nodes.name: bookings
nodes.summary: Session bookings storing the human booking_ref, package snapshot price, scheduling fields, deposit/remaining balance split, fully_paid flag and applied loyalty reward.

nodes.name: payments
nodes.summary: Payment records linked to a booking with amount, type, method, reference number, uploaded proof image, verification status, rejection reason and the staff member who verified it.

nodes.name: inventory
nodes.summary: Stock-keeping table of equipment and consumables with category, quantity and a low-stock threshold that drives the admin and staff inventory pages.

nodes.name: feedback
nodes.summary: Post-booking reviews with four separate rating dimensions, free-text comment, AI-derived sentiment and topics, and an is_urgent flag for negative-response escalation.

nodes.name: photos
nodes.summary: Uploaded gallery images tied to a booking and uploader, storing filename, filepath and a moderation status.

nodes.name: notifications
nodes.summary: In-app notification feed per user with a type discriminator, title, message, icon and is_read flag; backs the unread badge counted by sidebar.php and getUnreadCount().

nodes.name: loyalty_cards
nodes.summary: Per-user loyalty membership holding the card number, lifetime booking count, consumed reward count and card status.

nodes.name: settings
nodes.summary: Simple key/value store for admin-editable runtime settings, seeded with the business identity including the San Fernando and Camarines Sur location names.

nodes.name: password_resets
nodes.summary: Single-use password reset tokens keyed to a user and email with an expiry timestamp and a used flag, backing sendPasswordResetEmail().

nodes.name: .gitkeep
nodes.summary: Zero-byte placeholder that keeps the root uploads/ directory tracked by git. One of several scattered upload directories in this project and not itself written to by any code.

layers.name: Entry Points & Routing
layers.description: Web-reachable entry scripts for SnapTrack: index.php resolves index.php?page=<name> against the $rolePages allowlist and wraps pages in the layout shell, while landing.php, login.php, logout.php, google-login.php, google-callback.php and mfa-setup.php handle the public, credential, OAuth2 and TOTP enrollment flows.

layers.name: Shared Kernel
layers.description: The procedural core every other layer depends on: config.php (hand-rolled .env loading and constants) and functions.php (db(), ensureDatabaseSchema(), auth, CSRF, notifications, inventory, loyalty), plus the external-integration clients ai_helper.php (Gemini), send-verification.php (Resend/PHPMailer), mfa-helper.php (TOTP) and the unused includes/booking.php and includes/deduct_inventory.php.

layers.name: Presentation Shell
layers.description: The shared chrome included around every routed page - header.php (head, title, stylesheet link), sidebar.php (the $navAdmin/$navStaff/$navClient tables that must stay in sync with the router allowlist), footer.php (chatbot injection and asset loading) and the self-contained SnapBot chat widget in includes/chatbot.php.

layers.name: Admin Portal Pages
layers.description: Owner-facing router-loaded partials under pages/admin/ covering analytics and read-only oversight: the sales dashboard, 9-type reports module with PDF/CSV export, sales and payment ledgers, client segmentation, loyalty-card review, feedback triage with AI sentiment, package/inventory/staff/settings CRUD, plus the dead DFD.HTML design diagram.

layers.name: Studio Operations Pages
layers.description: Front-desk router-loaded partials under pages/staff/ that drive the daily session lifecycle: approve/complete/cancel booking transitions, walk-in creation with conflict detection and loyalty enrollment, on-site payment recording, payment proof verification and refunds, inventory CRUD, the schedule board, photo delivery uploads, client directory and notifications.

layers.name: Client Portal Pages
layers.description: Customer-facing router-loaded partials under pages/client/: self-service booking creation with overlap detection, booking list and cancellation, loyalty-aware dashboard, GCash/Maribank payment submission with proof upload, photo gallery, feedback submission, notification inbox and shared profile editing.

layers.name: JSON API Endpoints
layers.description: The pages/api/ endpoints, which unlike pages/<role>/ are standalone scripts that self-require config.php and functions.php and enforce their own session and role checks before emitting JSON: availability slot grids, loyalty lookup, on-site payment recording, client payment actions, inventory usage history, notification polling and the SnapBot AI cascade.

layers.name: Frontend Assets
layers.description: Client-side presentation and scaffolding: the one live stylesheet assets/css/styles.css that defines the 52-variable soft-gray design system, the live utilities in assets/js/app.js, the never-registered public/service-workers.js, and the unreferenced duplicates root styles.css, assets/images/css/styles.css and root app.js prototype.

layers.name: Database Schema & Seed Data
layers.description: sql/install.sql as a table node plus one node per CREATE TABLE it defines - users, packages, bookings, payments, inventory, feedback, photos, notifications, loyalty_cards, settings and password_resets - forming the single source of truth that ensureDatabaseSchema() in functions.php must be kept in sync with.

layers.name: Configuration, Ops Tooling & Docs
layers.description: Build and environment declarations (.env.example, composer.json, nixpacks.toml), the one-shot database tools that ship unauthenticated and must be removed before production (sql/install.php web installer, change_password.php bulk reset, sql/hash.php), and the agent-facing notes AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md that record the router allowlist and integration contracts.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: There is no README in this repository; GEMINI.md is the closest thing to one, describing the PHP 8.1 / MySQL stack, the pages/ layout split by role, and every external integration the app talks to (Gemini AI, Google OAuth plus TOTP MFA, PayMongo, PHPMailer, Resend, QR codes, TCPDF/FPDF). AGENTS.md sits alongside it with the engineering constraints a newcomer hits within the first hour: the router allowlist, the runtime schema mutation, and the fact that display_errors is off so fatals render as a blank page. Read both before touching code - the rest of this tour assumes their vocabulary.

tour.title: The Single Router
tour.description: index.php is the only authenticated entry point: every screen in the app is index.php?page=<name>. It loads config.php and functions.php, re-reads and re-validates the user from the database on every request, checks the page name against the per-role $rolePages allowlist, then resolves it through an ordered fallback chain (own role directory, then pages/<page>.php, then other role directories, then dashboard) and wraps the result in the header/sidebar/footer shell. Two consequences dominate everything downstream: files under pages/<role>/ are not standalone, because they assume the router already defined $user, $role and $page and calling requireRole() with no require_once of their own, and a page missing from the allowlist does not error - it silently redirects to the dashboard.
tour.languageLesson: PHP's require/include is runtime file inclusion rather than a module system, so a 'route' here is just a filesystem path. The router emulates a route table with an allowlist plus an ordered fallback chain of candidate paths, which is why adding a page touches three separate files and why a typo degrades silently instead of 404ing.

tour.title: Configuration and Environment
tour.description: config.php is the only reader of environment state and the first file both the router and every API endpoint load. Its hand-rolled loadEnv() parses .env into $_ENV and putenv(), which is why there is no dotenv dependency; DB_* values fall back to Railway-style MYSQLHOST/MYSQLPORT variables, and APP_URL is sniffed from request headers when unset. .env.example is the documented inventory of all 18 runtime variables - MySQL credentials, VAPID web-push keys, PayMongo, Google OAuth, Gemini, SMTP and Resend. Two sharp edges to carry forward: several define()s such as GEMINI_MODEL and UPLOAD_DIR are not environment-driven at all, and base-path detection only special-cases /snaptrack, so deploying under any other subfolder breaks every generated URL.
tour.languageLesson: The .env format is plain KEY=value lines. Most projects parse it with a dotenv library loaded through Composer autoloading; here it is reimplemented in PHP so the app can read secrets before anything else boots, with putenv() additionally exporting values to any child process or extension that reads the real environment.

tour.title: The Shared Kernel
tour.description: functions.php is the most depended-upon file in the graph by a wide margin, and the reason is that it is the app's entire shared surface: db(), session and currentUser(), requireRole(), the CSRF helpers, flash messages, notifications, loyalty tiers, inventory deduction and view helpers all live in this one procedural file. The decision worth understanding early is that the first db() call of every request triggers ensureDatabaseSchema(), which ALTERs missing columns and MODifies ENUMs on users, bookings, payments and packages - self-healing, so no migration file is ever needed, but also a schema that mutates at runtime and therefore needs ALTER privileges. Note that display_errors is switched off in this same file, so any fatal renders as a blank page and is written to php-errors.log instead.
tour.languageLesson: db() sets PDO's ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES to false, which sends parameter binding to MySQL for real. Values are bound, but identifiers (table and column names) can never be bound at all - that is why every query in this project interpolates only hard-coded identifiers and passes every user value through a bound parameter or cleanInt()/cleanFloat().

tour.title: The Data Model
tour.description: sql/install.sql is the source of truth: eleven CREATE TABLE statements followed by seed data for studio settings, demo users, packages, inventory, bookings and loyalty cards, with comments written in Filipino. users carries the identity story that Step 6 implements, holding role and active state, lockout tracking, email verification tokens, Google OAuth linkage, TOTP MFA secrets and bcrypt-hashed backup codes. packages self-references through parent_id to model sub-packages under a main package, and bookings stores a price snapshot plus a deposit / remaining-balance split so historic totals never shift when a catalogue price changes. payments then hangs off a booking with amount, type, method, reference number, uploaded proof image and verification status - the rows that Step 10 reconciles, and any column added here must also be added to ensureDatabaseSchema() from Step 4 or fresh and migrated installs diverge.
tour.languageLesson: This is a single bootstrap script rather than an ordered migration chain: it is not idempotent, so running it twice fails on CREATE TABLE. That is why the runtime ALTER-based upgrader in functions.php exists, and why the two representations must be edited together.

tour.title: Accounts, Email and MFA
